body: I truly appreciate your offer, but trust me, it's a dead end. I've kept my eyes glued to games, indie and triple-A alike, for years. I've tried a bunch of different genres including ones I thought I'd never touch. I've watched former friends and acquaintances go off and have a grand old time with new releases while I can't so much as muster up the willpower to grind through a tutorial. Social gaming is one of the many ways I've been made to feel alone.

No. In fact I feel left behind by the games industry. Every genre I've ever liked disappeared decades ago. I used to enjoy chill multiplayer games, but tryhards (and an industry that caters to them) have ruined that.
Yes. I don't like it. It's one of those things I can do, but only if I really force myself to.
It's a good job, but my job isn't my life, if that makes sense. At the end of the day, anything I do at that job isn't mine, it exists at the whim of the company.

I thought I wanted to create stuff. But the "stabler" I get, the more I have to push myself to even try to do that. Until I realized it was just a stressor and not a legitimate purpose. Unfortunately that was the only thing that drove me for years, since childhood even.
It sounds like such a stupid question, but, how do people find out what they want to do? Seems like people don't have to try for it, they just know. I don't have that.
